solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Respect maiden in a grave situation

indicators.note: in places the cricket abbreviation inside the words describing the grim plight

parts.note: a grave situation is a dire one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone salutes a young woman who is in serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, a close synonym of respecting them.

clue.text: Feeling guilty, so has made amends

indicators.note: amends read as the verb 'alters', so the letters of the words before it are changed around

explanation.surface: A remorseful person has tried to put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ashamed is the state of feeling guilt or embarrassment over what one has done.

clue.text: Lacking cryptic clue? Not important

parts.note: lacking something means minus it

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solver complains that a clue is missing, though it hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minuscule is tiny, so of trifling consequence: unimportant.

clue.text: Free beer, accepted and lifted, but put down again

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: to free someone of something is to rid them of it

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word for beer is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Free beer is taken and raised, then set back down on the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaid is the past tense of relay in the sense of laying again, like a floor or carpet put down a second time.

clue.text: With capital support he trades in a new way

indicators.note: doing something in a new way suggests rearranging, so the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: A businessman with funding behind him changes his trading methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial but means the head, as in capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital is a head, and a headrest is the cushion supporting it in a car seat or chair.

clue.text: Get out of doing something

parts.note: reads as dodging a task, but means to receive payment as a result of one's work

explanation.surface: Someone tries to wriggle out of a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain money or reward through work is exactly to obtain it from doing something.

clue.text: Name ship after European capitalist

indicators.note: after means the vessel follows the word for naming

parts.note: to dub is to name or title someone
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A tycoon from Europe has a vessel named after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' is not a financier but someone from a capital city: Dublin, Ireland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Dublin, a European capital city, is wittily called a capitalist.

clue.text: Pick hat up and finally leave

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the slang word for a hat is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone picks up their hat and at last goes home.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best members, its elite.

clue.text: Possibly pray when under the healing process

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the scrambled letters below the word the
possibly signals the letters of the next word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Prayer is suggested as a possible part of recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder.

clue.text: Held with an awkward grip

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is clutched clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is the part you grip, and a grip on a tool is its handle.

clue.text: Not straightforward, but giving a sign to the initiated

parts.note: the crab represents Cancer, a sign of the zodiac
those initiated into a secret are wise to it

explanation.surface: A secret society member makes an oblique signal to fellow insiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabwise means sideways, like a crab's walk, hence indirect rather than straight ahead.

clue.text: A slight but not trivial offence

definitions.meaning: a slight is a snub or insult
an offence given that is serious, an open insult

explanation.surface: A small snub is still no minor matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate insult, both a slight and a serious offence.

clue.text: Art master's pets are dogs

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, here with the possessive S
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a tiff

explanation.surface: A painting teacher keeps dogs as his pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals but means sulks: in a pet is in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a breed of large powerful guard dog.

clue.text: Pictures a mince pie

indicators.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A festive mince pie is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is not food here but the printing term for type spilled in a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is an old-fashioned name for the cinema, where films are shown.

clue.text: Land on a site needing development

indicators.note: needing development suggests the letters must be worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Building land on a plot awaiting construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a country, a land on the Baltic.

clue.text: Dead spirit to rap

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A dead spirit is made to knock, as at a seance.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to rap or tap repeatedly, as fingers on a table.

clue.text: In a way property is wealth

indicators.note: in a way signals the letters can be put another way, rearranged

explanation.surface: Owning property counts as being rich, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperity is the state of being wealthy or flourishing.

clue.text: Floods one sister with appointments

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun is a religious sister
dates are appointments to meet

explanation.surface: A nun is overwhelmed with engagements.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundates means floods, literally with water or figuratively with too much of something.

clue.text: Put on heavy music symbolic of Ireland

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for the noun, the plant that is the emblem

parts.note: to put on a show is to sham, to fake
heavy rock is loud music, so rock

explanation.surface: Fans fake their love of loud music on St Patrick's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the national emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Rocket engineer

parts.note: reads as a space scientist, but Rocket was the famous early steam locomotive of 1829

explanation.surface: A space-age rocket scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stephenson built the steam locomotive Rocket with his son Robert, not a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineer George Stephenson designed the pioneering railway locomotive called Rocket.

clue.text: Cloud cover is right in position

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the word for standing

parts.note: status is one's position or standing

explanation.surface: Cloud cover is correctly placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low flat sheet of grey cloud that blankets the sky.

clue.text: Insensitive one, for example, has no hesitation

indicators.note: has no means the hesitation sound is dropped

parts.note: one is an example of a number
er is the sound of a hesitation

explanation.surface: An unfeeling person speaks without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without feeling, insensitive to touch or emotion.

clue.text: Local supplier?

parts.note: local is British slang for a neighbourhood pub, which is supplied with beer

explanation.surface: A nearby shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, supplied by a beer maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer maker supplies pubs, the British 'locals'.

clue.text: On which to get wind of something|?

definitions.text: On which to get wind of something|?

parts.words: On which to get wind of something|
parts.note: reads as a source of rumour, but ... is British slang for the telephone, and a ... also blows wind

explanation.surface: A channel for picking up gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the telephone, where news is heard; a blower also produces wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The blower is old slang for the phone, the means of getting wind of news.

clue.text: Right to sue me, perhaps, so proceed

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters might be another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone defiantly says they are entitled to be sued, so go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to carry on, proceed after a pause.

clue.text: Composer right off his evening meal

indicators.note: off means the letter is taken away

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A composer has gone right off his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was a 19th-century Austrian composer of light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppé was an Austrian composer, best known for the Light Cavalry overture.

clue.text: Dogs, idle in disposition, have to be put out

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement, so the letters are placed afresh

explanation.surface: Lazy-natured dogs have to be turned outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of its position.

clue.text: Not a sign of a fatal wound

definitions.text: Not a sign of a fatal wound

parts.words: Not a sign of a fatal wound
parts.note: a mark left only by a wound that healed, so the victim survived

explanation.surface: No evidence of a deadly injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar remains only after a wound heals, so it marks one that was not fatal.

clue.text: Fine score with reverse snooker shot

indicators.note: reverse means the shot's word is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a snooker shot sinking a ball
to score is to cut a notch, also a tally

explanation.surface: A good result in snooker with a backspin shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch means excellent, of the finest quality.

clue.text: Sort of hats we put bands around

indicators.note: sort read as a verb, arranging, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Milliners fit ribbons round hats.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in bands of cloth.

clue.text: Sees rank out of line going on foot

definitions.note: a participial phrase describing things worn on the foot, standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: out of line means out of order, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An officer sees a soldier out of line marching.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneakers are soft shoes, things that go on the foot.

clue.text: Futile attempt to bury remains

indicators.note: to bury puts the remains inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Trying to hide the ashes is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy means worthless, of no value, like something futile.
